title: A temporary capital and a near-perfect average

questions.question: Before Parliament moved to Canberra in 1927, in which city did the federal Parliament sit?
questions.explanation: Federal Parliament met in Melbourne from 1901, borrowing the Victorian Parliament House. The Victorian Parliament moved to the Royal Exhibition Building in the meantime.

questions.question: Which is the largest Australian state or territory by area?
questions.explanation: Western Australia covers about 2.5 million square kilometres, close to a third of the country.

questions.question: What was Don Bradman's Test batting average when he retired?
questions.explanation: Bradman needed four runs in his final innings, at The Oval in 1948, to finish with an average of 100. He was bowled for a duck.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin aurum. Ag is silver, from argentum.
questions.source: Royal Society of Chemistry, Periodic Table

questions.question: Which architect designed the Sydney Opera House?
questions.explanation: The Danish architect won an international competition in 1957. He left the project in 1966 after a dispute with the NSW Government and never saw the finished building in person.

questions.question: In which year did Australia switch from pounds, shillings and pence to decimal currency?
questions.explanation: The dollar was introduced on 14 February 1966. Names considered for the new currency included the royal, the austral and the emu.

questions.question: Which band released the album Back in Black in 1980?
questions.explanation: It was AC/DC's first album with singer Brian Johnson, recorded months after the death of Bon Scott. It is one of the best-selling albums ever made.
questions.source: National Film and Sound Archive of Australia

questions.question: How many bones are there in a typical adult human body?
questions.explanation: Babies are born with around 300 bones and pieces of cartilage, many of which fuse as they grow.

questions.question: Canberra is the capital of Australia. What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa was chosen in 1857, partly as a compromise between larger rival cities. Canberra exists for much the same reason.

questions.question: Who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, in December 1911?
questions.explanation: The Norwegian's party arrived on 14 December 1911, about five weeks ahead of Scott's. Mawson, the Australian, was leading a separate scientific expedition at the time.
